successCriteria.description: LeaveBalanceService.initializeBalance resolves the active policy for the given leaveTypeId via ILeavePolicyService.getActivePolicy, and when a policy is found, persists a new LeaveBalance row with totalEntitlement sourced from the policy's entitlementDays, usedDays=0, pendingDays=0, status='ACTIVE', and the returned balance's remainingDays equals totalEntitlement (computed, never written).

LeaveBalanceService.deductDays rejects (throws a typed error) when totalEntitlement - usedDays - days < 0, and otherwise atomically increments usedDays via the repository and returns the updated balance whose remainingDays reflects the new totalEntitlement - usedDays.
LeaveBalanceService.restoreDays atomically decrements usedDays via the repository and returns the updated balance whose remainingDays reflects the recomputed totalEntitlement - usedDays.

LeaveBalanceService.getBalance and getAllBalances delegate to the repository and return balances whose remainingDays is computed as totalEntitlement - usedDays at query time (matching the repository's rowToLeaveBalance computation), never read from a stored column.

NotificationService exposes four notifyLeave<Event> methods (submitted, approved, rejected, cancelled) each accepting a LeaveRequestDTO and resolving to void without throwing; the stub logs to console and performs no external I/O.

The leave-balance barrel (index.ts) exports the new ILeaveBalanceService interface and LeaveBalanceService class in addition to the existing model and repository exports, and the notification barrel exports INotificationService and NotificationService, enabling cross-module consumption through index.ts only.

The two new test files (leave-balance.service.spec.ts and notification.service.spec.ts) pass under Jest with mocked repository/service dependencies, verifying the balance computation, deduct guard, restore, initialize-from-policy, and notification logging behavior.

constraints: No audit injection in Phase 9 — LeaveBalanceService constructor takes only ILeaveBalanceRepository and ILeavePolicyService; audit wiring is deferred to Phase 10. GP-002 audit records are not written by this phase's services.

remainingDays is read-only/computed: it must never be passed as a create/update input to the repository. The repository's create input type already omits remainingDays and lists it in READ_ONLY_FIELDS; the service must rely on rowToLeaveBalance to compute it at read time.

Cross-module imports go through barrel index.ts files only — LeaveBalanceService must import ILeavePolicyService from the leave-policy barrel (src/modules/leave-policy/index.ts), not from internal service files. Same-module imports (LeaveBalance model, ILeaveBalanceRepository) use internal files directly.

NotificationService is a console-logging stub with no constructor dependencies; it imports only LeaveRequestDTO from src/shared/types/index.ts. The dependency-map edge notification → employee is for the future real implementation, not this stub phase.

Strict TypeScript (no-any rule): use unknown with type guards instead of any. No direct database access outside the repository layer (GP-001) — the service must not import the pg pool or write SQL. All async errors must be caught/handled (GP-006).

The two new test files use the .spec.ts extension (task override of the .test.ts project convention); Jest config matches both patterns. Tests use jest.Mocked and factory helpers with relative imports resolving four levels up from tests/unit/modules/<module>/.
outOfScope: Audit record creation for balance deduct/restore/initialize operations — deferred to Phase 10 (leave-request orchestration) which injects IAuditRepository.

Real email/SMS notification delivery — NotificationService is a console-logging stub only; actual transport, employee/manager recipient resolution, and the notification → employee dependency are deferred to a later phase.
LeaveRequest service, controller, routes, and business-day utility — Phase 10 scope. This phase does not build the leave-request orchestration layer that consumes these services.

Balance status transitions (ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED → FROZEN) and pendingDays manipulation — the service initializes with status='ACTIVE' and pendingDays=0; EXHAUSTED/FROZEN lifecycle transitions and pending-day reservation logic are not implemented in this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: remainingDays is always derived as totalEntitlement - usedDays at read time and is never persisted or written through any create/update path; every balance returned by the service must satisfy remainingDays === totalEntitlement - usedDays.

A newly initialized balance has usedDays=0, pendingDays=0, status='ACTIVE', and totalEntitlement equal to the active policy's entitlementDays for the given leaveTypeId; the policyId on the balance must reference the policy that was active at initialization time.

usedDays must never become negative and must never exceed totalEntitlement as a result of service operations: deductDays is rejected before any mutation when totalEntitlement - usedDays - days < 0, and restoreDays must not drive usedDays below zero.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must throw a typed error when no active policy exists for the given leaveTypeId (getActivePolicy returns null); on success returns a persisted LeaveBalance with status ACTIVE and entitlement sourced from the policy.

Must throw a typed error when the balance does not exist for the employee/type/year combination, or when totalEntitlement - usedDays - days < 0 (insufficient remaining); on success atomically increments usedDays and returns the updated balance.
Must throw a typed error when the balance does not exist for the employee/type/year combination; on success atomically decrements usedDays and returns the updated balance.

Must resolve to void without throwing for all four event variants (submitted, approved, rejected, cancelled); the stub logs to console and performs no external I/O, so no transient-failure retry semantics apply.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The service's remainingDays computation must match the repository's rowToLeaveBalance formula exactly: remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays (not totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays). The repository already computes this at read time; the service must not recompute or override it with a different formula.

The service must call the repository's atomic incrementUsedDays/decrementUsedDays methods for deduct/restore (which use UPDATE ... SET used_days = used_days +/- $n) rather than read-modify-write via update(); this preserves the atomic counter semantics established in Phase 4.

The service must never include remainingDays in the create input passed to the repository — the repository's create signature is Omit<LeaveBalance, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt' | 'remainingDays'> and remainingDays is in READ_ONLY_FIELDS, so any attempt to write it would be silently dropped or cause a type error.

initializeBalance must source totalEntitlement and policyId from the LeavePolicy returned by ILeavePolicyService.getActivePolicy(leaveTypeId) — specifically policy.entitlementDays and policy.id — matching the field names established in the leave-policy model and service interface.

NotificationService methods must accept the LeaveRequestDTO shape as defined in shared-types (id, employeeId, leaveTypeId, startDate, endDate, reason?, rejectionReason?, status, approvedBy, approvedAt, cancelledAt, createdAt, updatedAt) — imported from the shared-types barrel, not redefined locally.

The leave-balance barrel update must mirror the leave-policy barrel pattern: export both the service interface (ILeaveBalanceService) and the service class (LeaveBalanceService) alongside the existing model and repository exports, so cross-module consumers import through index.ts only.

integrationPoints.why: LeaveBalanceService.initializeBalance depends on the leave-policy service to resolve the active policy for a leaveTypeId, sourcing policyId and entitlementDays for the new balance. This is the leave-balance → leave-policy dependency edge.

LeaveBalanceService delegates all persistence (create, findByEmployeeAndType, findByEmployee, incrementUsedDays, decrementUsedDays) to the existing repository interface from Phase 4; no direct DB access.
NotificationService imports LeaveRequestDTO from the shared-types barrel as the parameter type for all four notify methods; this is the notification → shared-types dependency edge.

Phase 10's LeaveRequestService will consume both new services: initializeBalance/deductDays on submit, restoreDays on reject/cancel, and the four notification methods on each lifecycle transition. The interfaces and barrel exports produced here are the contract Phase 10 depends on.
